name: Ten Yard Fight
label: Equal Vision
lede: A Boston youth crew band whose singer played the first show in football gear, who fired a guitarist for wanting to stop singing about football, and whose last show, on a Red Sox playoff night, became straight edge's own holiday.

eras.title: Shoulder pads and circle pits
eras.text: Ten Yard Fight started as something close to a joke: a straight edge band with a football theme and a singer in pads. The joke sold a thousand demos and a 7" that vanished in days, and the band started taking itself seriously, some members more than others.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight's first show: Anthony Moreschi in football gear
years.p: Singer Anthony "Wrench" Moreschi plays Ten Yard Fight's first show in a mix of football gear and punk clothes, with John LaCroix on bass. The crowd loves it.
Ten Yard Fight record their first demo in October 1995 at Salad Days Studio. According to Bridge 9 and Wikipedia it sells 1,000 copies, a real number for a new Boston hardcore band.

Ten Yard Fight's debut 7", recorded in March 1996 at Salad Days with [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]], comes out on Boston's Big Wheel Recreation. Wikipedia says the first pressing sold out in under a week.
Ten Yard Fight share a 7" with Fastbreak, and the success of Hardcore Pride lands them a deal with Equal Vision.

q: They made me show up to practice, then they kicked me out.
years.h: Ten Yard Fight kick out guitarist Anthony Pappalardo
years.p: Guitarist Anthony Pappalardo wants Ten Yard Fight to stop writing about football and bragging about straight edge. The band calls him to practice and fires him there.
years.xp:
Pappalardo told No Echo the band later told people he couldn't play guitar. Within two months he and Sweet Pete had started [[In My Eyes|f8a4cb28-0443-48af-b58a-b2b2ab51206d]].

He also rejected the youth crew revival tag, saying the band drew on Samiam, [[Turning Point|19b7cbc9-0898-400a-87d5-bfa47c87487c]] and [[Inside Out|0049c4d7-6459-4b54-a865-fd19969f427f]] as much as [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]].

eras.title: Back on track
eras.text: In 1997 Ten Yard Fight, In My Eyes and Floorpunch brought back the late-'80s youth crew sound, and Equal Vision put out the record that led the charge. The band toured the US and Europe hard, and the line-up never sat still.

years.h: Equal Vision's Hardcore Pride CD adds the demo and a Brotherhood cover
years.p: Equal Vision's first Ten Yard Fight release puts the Hardcore Pride EP, Demo '95 and a cover of Brotherhood on one CD.

years.h: Back on Track, Ten Yard Fight's Equal Vision album
years.p: Recorded in March 1997 at Salad Days with Brian McTernan: Moreschi, Chris Patterson on guitar, John LaCroix on bass and Ben Chused on drums. It spearheads the 1997 youth crew revival.

years.h: [[Aaron Dalbec|5ea0f2e5-66d0-48ce-82d5-9c85d2fa4c39]] plays second guitar live; Ben Chused joins [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]]
years.p: The Back on Track credits list Aaron Dalbec, of [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] and Bane, as Ten Yard Fight's second guitarist at live shows. Drummer Ben Chused plays in Bane from 1997 to 1998.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight tour Europe and the US and reshuffle
years.p: Ten Yard Fight spend 1997 and 1998 touring Europe and the US. By the end, Tim Cossar is on guitar, John LaCroix has moved from bass to guitar, and Brian "Clevo" Ristau plays bass.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight record The Only Way in Gloucester
years.p: Ten Yard Fight cut six songs at Impact Studios in Gloucester, Massachusetts, produced by Dean Baltulonis and Matt Henderson.

eras.title: Game day at the Karma Club
eras.text: Ten Yard Fight ended on a Boston Sunday with their friends on the bill and a playoff game at Fenway down the street. The date became a holiday.

years.h: The Only Way EP, Ten Yard Fight's last studio record
years.p: Equal Vision issues The Only Way (EVR 49), the final line-up's only record. The CD has a seventh song, No Place, left off the 7".

q: I think we did way more than we ever set out to do.
years.src: Wikipedia: National Edge Day · Bridge 9 · No Echo (2020)
years.h: Ten Yard Fight's last show becomes the first Edge Day
years.p: Ten Yard Fight play their final show at the Karma Club on Lansdowne Street, next to Fenway, on a day of the American League Championship Series. [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]], Reach the Sky and In My Eyes play too.
years.xp:
The show, first billed as Edge Fest, is counted as the first National Edge Day. Straight edge kids now mark it every year, from Atlanta and Santa Ana to Gothenburg, London and Kuala Lumpur.

Anthony Moreschi filmed it: he told No Echo the final show was his first real video project.

yt: Ten Yard Fight: The Only Way video documentary
years.h: The Only Way: 1995–1999, a Ten Yard Fight video history
years.p: A documentary video of Ten Yard Fight's run, built around the final show, comes out as the band's last release.

years.src: Wikipedia · The Punk Rock MBA · No Echo (2020)
years.h: After Ten Yard Fight: [[American Nightmare|f73634fa-c89b-4bc3-8cd0-81891bcafa9e]], Stand and Fight, magazines
years.p: Tim Cossar forms American Nightmare. Anthony Moreschi moves to Southern California and later fronts Stand and Fight on Bridge 9. John LaCroix starts the art magazine While You Were Sleeping with the band's roadie, Roger Gastman.
years.xp:
LaCroix and Gastman later started Swindle with Shepard Fairey; LaCroix went on to be a creative director, including on the NFL's first-down-line graphics, and played in Unrestrained.

Wikipedia also credits LaCroix with the first documented 'edge confession' letter, written after he broke edge sometime between 2000 and 2005.

eras.title: Edge Day, every year
eras.text: The band that gave straight edge its holiday kept turning up for it. Moreschi and Ristau played as First and Ten, the band returned for This Is Hardcore, and in 2025 they said yes to Furnace Fest.

years.h: First and Ten play National Edge Day in Haverhill
years.p: Anthony Moreschi and Brian Ristau reunite as First and Ten at National Edge Day 2007 in Haverhill, Massachusetts.

years.h: First and Ten share a bill with [[Slapshot|efc798e2-3165-49fd-a83b-d659cdb20488]]
years.p: Moreschi and Ristau's First and Ten, Ten Yard Fight in all but name, play again with Boston's Slapshot.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight headline night one of This Is Hardcore
years.p: Ten Yard Fight's original line-up reunites to headline the first day of This Is Hardcore 2018 in Philadelphia.

years.h: Anthony Moreschi's hardcore and BMX series Don't Stand in Line
years.p: Emmy-winning filmmaker Anthony Moreschi, Ten Yard Fight's singer, makes Don't Stand in Line, a six-part series on DIY ethics in hardcore, BMX and skating, featuring Bridge 9's Chris Wrenn and hate5six's Sunny Singh.

years.h: Ten Yard Fight reunite for Furnace Fest
years.p: Announced in February 2025 alongside A Change of Pace, Ten Yard Fight's Furnace Fest set in Birmingham, Alabama was billed by Lambgoat as their return after almost thirty years.
